title: A Choir for the Oath
premise: Ivo Eastwick has spent her life in the Valley of the Vow, a place sealed against magic, where she serves as the king's food-taster, dosing herself daily with poisons to build the immunity her survival depends on. When a mute child arrives speaking a dead tongue, Ivo discovers the valley's seal was her own grandmother's doing—a covenant that has kept magic out but is now strangling the world beyond, and the child is its living key. To reforge the covenant, Ivo must leave the valley, surrender the immunity that defines her, and face the poisoner who has been slowly killing her king from inside the court. In the end, Ivo chooses to bind herself as the new living seal, trading her freedom and her budding love for the court archivist for the world's survival, while the child carries her name back into a realm that can finally breathe.
about_author: I. M. Iversen is a former archivist of medieval charters who writes fantasy from a converted lighthouse on the northern coast. Their work is known for quiet, domestic magic and characters who discover that small lives were never small.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. We learn the rhythm of her life: tasting, dosing, enduring the numbness spreading through her hands. When the child appears at the valley gate, speaking a language Ivo somehow half-understands, the seal flickers visibly for the first time in a generation. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine—the first crack in a life built on invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Grandmother Swallowed
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with the archivist Wren's letters interspersed. Searching her grandmother's effects, Ivo finds the covenant's terms: a living seal must hold it, and the seal is dying. The child's presence means magic is already leaking through. Ivo realizes her poison-immunity is no accident—she was bred and dosed for this inheritance. The emotional beat is betrayal curdling into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: Beyond the Valley of the Vow
chapters.summary: Ivo and the child cross the seal; Wren follows against orders. Outside, magic floods back into Ivo's body, and with it every poison she has ever tasted, burning through her immunity. In the capital they uncover the court poisoner—a rival heir's agent who has been feeding the king slow death and now hunts the child. The emotional beat is love acknowledged in the worst possible hour, as Wren and Ivo confess what they cannot afford to want.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Oath
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing with Wren's. At the ruined covenant-stone, Ivo takes the poisoner's final dose willingly, letting it become the binding agent of a new oath sung by the child in the old tongue. She becomes the seal—alive, conscious, held. The emotional beat is grief transfigured: Wren reads to her at the stone each year, and the valley's silence becomes, at last, a kind of music.
